message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations: | Area | Key Points | |------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate highways: 75 mph (or 70 mph if posted).
• Urban freeways: 65 mph (or 55 mph if posted).
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours; 35 mph after. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine plus points on the driver’s record. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Violations carry a $100 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol education, and possible jail time.
• First offense: up to 90 days in jail, $500–$2,000 fine. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light: stop before the line; proceed only when green.
• Stop sign: full stop at the intersection; yield to pedestrians and other vehicles.
• Yield sign: slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians always have priority at crosswalks. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep within lane markings; avoid weaving.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a no‑stop zone is prohibited. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in). | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 total per accident, $25,000 property damage.
• Proof of insurance must be carried in the vehicle. | ### How to Find Recent Traffic‑Related Lawsuits in Texas If you’re interested in recent legal cases involving traffic violations or road safety issues, I can run a quick search. Let me know the specific topic (e.g., “speeding,” “cell‑phone use,” “pedestrian accidents”) and the year you’d like to focus on.
